subject: Reservation flex-lane sizing & quantization fit assessment
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie@brightframe.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightframe.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Brightframe RFP: reservation sizing + flex/burst question

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking this RFP — appreciate you and your team. Attaching our workload profile and a short set of latency/throughput targets. High level: we plan to serve a mix of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) agents and batch embedding jobs. Key asks:

- Recommend a reserved capacity commitment (GPU types + count) that meets 99th p50 latency targets for chat (p50 ~ 180ms token) for peak window (7–9AM PST) and average embedding throughput targets (30k embeddings/hr)
- Describe an architecture for a "flex lane" (we call it burst buffer) to handle 3x short bursts per day without impacting reserved SLOs
- Quantization fit: can you say which models and quantization levels you recommend to meet cost/latency trade-offs?

Files: Brightframe_RFP_Workload_Profile.xlsx (workload by route + traces), bf_sample_traces.tar.gz

Can your sizing include both a base reserved pool and a recommended burst lane configuration (preemptible vs reserved spare)? Hoping for an initial sketch this week.

Thanks,
Jamie Park
Director, Infrastructure Procurement
Brightframe AI

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@brightframe.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightframe RFP: reservation sizing + flex/burst question

Hi Jamie — thanks for the profile and traces, received them. Quick plan from our side:

1) Clarify a couple small items (if you can confirm by EOD PST):
   - How many concurrent RAG sessions during peak do you expect? (your workbook lists sessions/hr but not concurrent active sessions)
   - What percentage of requests will be max-sequence (4k tokens) versus short-turns (<=256 tokens)?

2) We'll put together an initial sizing that includes: base reserved pool (GPU types + count), a recommended flex/burst lane (preemptible + hot-cache guidance), and suggested quantization levels per model family.

3) Proposed workshop: 30–45m technical sizing session Wed 23 Jun 2027 10:00–10:45AM PST. Ben (solutions) and Laura (capacity planning) will join. Are you available?

I'll circulate an initial workbook by Thu morning.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Solutions 
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: initial flex-lane sizing notes for Brightframe

Chloe / Laura — notes from my quick pass through the traces and workbook:

- Workload mix estimate (derived): RAG chat 62%, embeddings batch 28%, rerank/other 10%
- Suggested reserved GPU mix (starting point):
   * 4 x A10G (good baseline for 4k context, cost-efficient for steady RAG)
   * 2 x H100s (for high-throughput embedding offload and heavy-model experiments)
- Flex/burst lane approach ("flex-lane"):
   * Keep a small warm pool (1-2 A10G equiv) pinned to cache critical KV prefixes for session warm-up
   * Configure burst lane as preemptible H100s or spot Gpus with auto-fallback to a smaller quantized model on A10G if preempted
   * Throttle policy: cap burst to no more than 3x baseline for windows >30s to avoid cache thrash
- Quantization recommendations: prefer Q4_K or Q4_0 for chat models to balance latency/quality; use Q5/Q6 experiments on H100 for embeddings if you need maximal throughput

Open items for the workshop: concurrent sessions, tail-latency SLO at p99 (we need their p99 target), and whether they have any firm contract term for reserved commit (12 or 36 months).

I'll draft the sizing workbook skeleton and push to the Drive link Chloe mentioned.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Park <jamie@brightframe.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightframe.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightframe RFP: reservation sizing + flex/burst question

Thanks Chloe / Ben — Wed 10:00 works for us. Quick clarifications (answers to your questions):

- Expected concurrent RAG sessions in peak: ~180 active sessions (concurrent), with average turn length 310 tokens; ~12% of requests hit the 4k context.
- Embedding batch pattern: 60% steady background jobs, 40% hourly spikes (up to 8k/hr for 15–30m windows)
- p99 tail target for chat token latency: 650ms (we can stretch to 800ms for very large prompts)

I've attached a small sample traces archive and added a short procurement note: we prefer a 12-month committed term but are evaluating 36-month pricing for comparison. We'll want to see both.

Files: bf_sample_traces.tar.gz

Looking forward to the workshop. Please include any pre-read or estimation workbook so procurement can route internally.

Best,
Jamie

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@brightframe.ai>, procurement@brightframe.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: draft flex-lane sizing workbook + next steps

Jamie — thanks again for the quick answers during the workshop. Attached is our draft sizing workbook and a short narrative with assumptions. High-level summary:

- Base reserved pool recommendation (12-mo and 36-mo columns included):
   * 6 x A10G (steady-state RAG), 2 x H100 (embedding offload) — this hits your p50/p99 targets at current load with Q4_K quantization on chat models
   * If you opt for 36-month commitment, switch 2 A10G -> 2 A100S (cost per token decreases ~14% in our model)
- Flex-lane design: 3x burst capacity via preemptible H100s + 1 warm A10G pool for KV/prefix cache. Auto-fallback rule: if a preemptible drops, traffic re-routes to quantized A10G instances with reduced max-context to preserve tail SLOs.
- Cost/latency tradeoffs: workbook includes token-level cost simulation for Q4_0 vs Q4_K vs FP16 weights on H100 for embeddings.

Attachments: redwood-flexlane-sizing-workbook.xlsx (Drive link also below).

Next steps:
- Please review the workbook and confirm if you want 12- or 36-month pricing options modeled in more detail by Tue 29 Jun.
- If you want, we can schedule a handoff call with procurement + legal to walk the commitment terms.

Drive pre-read: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_workbook
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/BRI-2027-045

Regards,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
